sources.title: TN MAWS Policy Note (annual, budget session)
sources.publisher: TN Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department

provenance.note: Status changes only with a dated citation; per-commitment citations inline (commitment_source + status_history entries). update_model names the annual MAWS Policy Note, ADB project documents and dated press as the re-check set.

headline: 16 commitments on Chennai's register: 5 delivered, including two big treatment plants, 1 on track, and 10 in progress or awaiting a dated record, 3 of them with no completion date given.
intro: Dated commitments by the institutions that manage this city's water - CMWSSB, the MAWS department, the state government and the courts that set deadlines for them - made to residents, courts and funders, and followed from announcement to delivery. Every commitment carries its original citation and every status change carries a dated source. A commitment completed after its date is recorded as delivered, with both dates shown, and when a date moves, the earlier one stays on the record. Each status rests on the institutions' own documents or on dated reporting.

status_legend.delivered: A dated source records completion. The original date and the completion date are both shown.
status_legend.on-track: The stated date has not passed and the latest dated evidence is consistent with it.
status_legend.slipped: The institution itself has moved the date. Old and new dates are both shown.
status_legend.overdue: The promised date has passed with no delivery and no formally revised date we can cite.
status_legend.stalled: Work or approvals have stopped, by the institution's own account or a court's.
status_legend.unverified: We can cite the promise but cannot yet cite its current status either way.

commitments.title: 100% metering of high-rise and commercial connections by 2023; 80% of domestic by 2027
commitments.committed_by: CMWSSB Board (Metering Policy resolution of 23 November 2022, under the World Bank Chennai City Partnership)
commitments.what: CMWSSB's board-approved metering policy set two targets: every high-rise and commercial connection metered by 2023, and 80% of ordinary domestic connections by 2027. As of May 2025, 3.12% of the city's 7.7 lakh connections had functioning meters (24,095). A 1-lakh smart-meter DBFOT package was announced with tender expected May 2025 and two-year installation, and the commercial/high-rise target was re-based to 90% by 2025-26. The same policy note carries an undated goal of cutting non-revenue water below 15%.

commitment_source.label: MAWS Policy Note 2023-24, p.357 (CMWSSB Metering Policy, board resolution 23 Nov 2022)

status_history.note: 3.12% of 7.7 lakh connections metered (24,095 functioning meters) as of May 2025; the policy's date for high-rise and commercial connections was December 2023. CMWSSB announces a 1-lakh smart-meter package (73,000 domestic in large buildings + 27,000 commercial/institutional), tender expected May 2025, with slab tariffs of Rs 6-45 per kilolitre.
status_history.source_label: DT Next, 24 May 2025

status_history.note: The 1-lakh smart-meter package is awarded to a concessionaire: JWIL Infra, Rs 273.60 crore under a hybrid annuity model. Meter fixing expected to begin by December 2026 (a November 2025 report had given a December 2025 start) and the metering network to be completed by August 2028; the policy's original date for high-rises and commercial connections was 2023.
status_history.source_label: The Hindu (Chennai), 23 Jun 2026, via PressReader

status_history.note: The state's MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (section 5.8, Chennai City Partnership Programme, DLI 7) records the metering policy as approved and adopted by the Board; IoT bulk water meters at treatment plants and distribution stations, with completion including a dashboard expected by August 2026; and the installation of 1 lakh meters for high-volume consumers in multi-storied buildings, commercial and partly commercial consumers as 'Work under progress'. The note gives no completion date for the 1 lakh meters.
status_history.source_label: MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (Demand No. 34), Government of Tamil Nadu, Aug 2026, pp.224-225 (section 5.8, DLI 7)

commitments.title: Perur 400 MLD desalination plant by December 2026
commitments.committed_by: CMWSSB / Government of Tamil Nadu; JICA-funded; built by VA Tech Wabag + Metito
commitments.what: Chennai's fourth and largest desal plant: 400 MLD at Perur on East Coast Road, for ~22.67 lakh people in south Chennai and Tambaram. Foundation stone laid by CM M.K. Stalin on 21-22 August 2023; the 42-month EPC contract implied completion by December 2026. In February 2026 the official line was commissioning by March 2027, with trial runs from around September 2026; the state's MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 gives completion and commissioning by October 2027. Cost appears as Rs 4,276 crore (the plant contract) and Rs 6,078 crore (the full sanctioned project including the 59 km transmission main to Porur), figures at different scopes; the 2026-27 note gives an estimated cost of Rs 5,814.57 crore (p.200).

commitment_source.label: Business Standard, 21 Aug 2023 (foundation stone); Dec 2026 target per Indian Infrastructure, 25 Jan 2024

status_history.note: The MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 (p.305) records that the plant 'is expected to be completed and commissioned by February 2027', later than the December 2026 date. Entry dated by the note's PDF.
status_history.source_label: MAWS Policy Note 2025-26, p.305

status_history.note: Construction reaches 42% completion.
status_history.source_label: Indian Infrastructure, 28 Jul 2025

status_history.note: Around 62% complete; trial run expected by September 2026; completion revised to March 2027. CMWSSB MD T.G. Vinay separately put it at 'around 60%' with commissioning 'by March 2027' (DT Next, 11 Feb 2026).
status_history.source_label: Indian Infrastructure, 13 Feb 2026

status_history.note: Checked 18 Oct 2026. The MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (section 5.2.1) states that the 400 MLD plant, at an estimated cost of Rs.5,814.57 crore with assistance from JICA, the Tamil Nadu Infrastructure Development Fund and State budgetary support, 'is under construction and expected to be completed and commissioned by October 2027'. The 2025-26 note had given February 2027, against an administrative sanction of Rs 6,078.40 crore that included the product water transmission main (p.305), and CMWSSB gave March 2027 in February 2026. October 2027 has not passed. The Chief Minister inspected the works on 6 July 2026 and directed officials to expedite them (DT Next, 6 Jul 2026). The trial run expected from September 2026 has no dated record yet in the sources checked.
status_history.source_label: MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (Demand No. 34), Government of Tamil Nadu, Aug 2026, p.200 (section 5.2.1); 2025-26 note, p.305

status_history.note: CMWSSB's Contingency Plan for North-East Monsoon 2026 records construction of the 400 MLD plant as under progress, with scheduled completion in October 2027.
status_history.source_label: CMWSSB Contingency Plan 2026, p.2

commitments.title: Nemmeli II 150 MLD desalination plant by December 2021
commitments.committed_by: CMWSSB / Government of Tamil Nadu; KfW + AMRUT funded; built by Cobra-Tecton consortium
commitments.what: Chennai's third desal plant: 150 MLD inside the existing Nemmeli campus with a ~47.6 km conveyance line to Pallavaram, for ~9 lakh people in south Chennai. Contract awarded 27 May 2019 (Rs 1,689 crore including 20-year O&M) with completion promised by December 2021. It was inaugurated on 24 February 2024, about 26 months after the contract's completion date of December 2021; government documents revised the date three times before then.

commitment_source.label: Contract award to Cobra-Tecton, 27 May 2019, completion Dec 2021 (DMS Universe project record; corroborated by CMWSSB's project document recording the Dec-2021 pipeline contract horizon)

status_history.note: The government's National Infrastructure Pipeline portal revises expected completion to 27 April 2023.
status_history.source_label: India Investment Grid (NIP project 607750), status updated 28 Mar 2022

status_history.note: MAWS Policy Note 2023-24 says the scheme is 'expected to be completed by July 2023'.
status_history.source_label: MAWS Policy Note 2023-24, p.322-323

status_history.note: Inaugurated by CM M.K. Stalin, about 26 months after the contract's completion date of December 2021.
status_history.source_label: Tedagua (Grupo Cobra) press note, 27 Feb 2024

status_history.note: The state's MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (section 5.1.1) records the 150 MLD Nemmeli plant as established in 2024 at a cost of Rs 1,516.82 crore, supplying added areas in southern Chennai and Tambaram Corporation for a population of 9 lakh.
status_history.source_label: MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (Demand No. 34), Government of Tamil Nadu, Aug 2026, p.196 (section 5.1.1)

commitments.title: Revamp the Minjur 100 MLD desalination plant (no date given)
commitments.what: Minjur was India's first large desal plant: promised for January 2009 under a 2005 concession with Chennai Water Desalination Ltd, and commissioned in July 2010, about 18 months later, after cyclone damage. After output and quality 'deteriorated considerably', CMWSSB issued a termination order on 24 September 2024, about a decade before the concession's 2035 end. The board has announced a revamp: a consultant-led assessment 'within 30 days' of appointment and a DPR. The state's MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 records that CMWSSB took over the plant's operation on 1 April 2025 and is refurbishing it in phases to start production at an interim 20 MLD, with a DPR for full restoration under preparation. No date has been given for restoring the full 100 MLD.

commitment_source.label: DT Next, 5 Jul 2025 ('Chennai Metro Water Board plans to revamp Minjur desalination plant')

status_history.note: The termination is on court record: in Madras High Court Section 9 proceedings, CMWSSB states it terminated CWDL's contract and seeks to take possession of the Kattupalli/Minjur plant and run it itself.
status_history.source_label: Madras HC Section 9 proceeding, CMWSSB v Chennai Water Desalination Ltd (~Mar 2025, via Casemine)

status_history.note: CMWSSB confirms it terminated the CWDL contract after output and quality deteriorated and the operator took no corrective action; revamp DPR planned, tender 'to be floated soon', no completion date. Press claims of a November 2024 full shutdown and partial resumption at 20 MLD could not be verified in any citable source and are excluded.
status_history.source_label: DT Next, 5 Jul 2025

status_history.note: Madras High Court appoints Justice K.R. Shriram (retired, former Chief Justice of the Madras HC) as sole arbitrator over the disputes under the Bulk Water Purchase Agreement of 13 September 2005. The dispute is now in arbitration; no date has yet been given for restoring north Chennai's 100 MLD. The state's MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 lists Minjur at 100 MLD; the 2026-27 note records the termination and the takeover (next entry).
status_history.source_label: Madras HC order, 13 Oct 2025 (Indian Kanoon)

status_history.note: Checked 18 Oct 2026. The MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (section 5.1.1) records that CMWSSB issued a termination order to the operator on 24.09.2024 and, under Madras High Court orders, 'assumed control and operation of the plant on 01.04.2025'. It states that 'Refurbishment and restoration works are being carried out in a phased manner to commence production initially at an interim capacity of 20 MLD', and that a DPR for full restoration 'is under preparation'. It gives no date. A CMWSSB official told DT Next (3 Sep 2026) that partial production of 20 MLD was likely in October 2026 and full capacity by the end of 2026. The note records the work as under way, so the row moves from stalled to unverified until a dated output or progress figure can be cited.
status_history.source_label: MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (Demand No. 34), Government of Tamil Nadu, Aug 2026, pp.194-195

commitments.title: Chennai Ring Main: 97.9 km bulk-water loop, construction June 2026 to May 2030
commitments.committed_by: CMWSSB / Government of Tamil Nadu, ADB-financed (project 59311-001)
commitments.what: A closed loop of large-diameter mains around Greater Chennai connecting all major treatment plants and reservoirs, so any source can feed any zone at balanced pressure - billed as the first comprehensive ring main in an Indian city. CMWSSB's environmental examination (March 2026) commits to construction from June 2026 to May 2030, a six-month trial, and commissioning by November 2030. Bids were opened 3 February 2026 and ADB approved a $230 million loan in early July 2026. No contract award had been reported as of July 2026; the state's MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 records the project as under implementation, to be completed by 2031.

commitment_source.label: CMWSSB Initial Environmental Examination for ADB, March 2026, para 49 (construction Jun 2026 - May 2030, trial to Nov 2030)

status_history.note: ADB approves a $230 million loan for the project (170+ km of water and sewer pipelines, 7 water pumping stations, 38 sewer pumping stations, 4.5 million beneficiaries). Cost figures on record conflict: Minister K.N. Nehru cited Rs 2,000 crore allocated (Mar 2025) and 'Rs 3,500 crore project' (Jul 2025) - likely allocation versus total, unresolved in sources.
status_history.source_label: PSU Watch, 3 Jul 2026

status_history.note: The state's MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (section 5.2.4) records the ring main for the Greater Chennai Corporation area, about 98 km, as under implementation at a cost of Rs 3,108.55 crore with ADB assistance and 'to be completed by 2031', and proposed for partial funding under the Urban Challenge Fund. The March 2026 environmental examination gave commissioning by November 2030; both dates are shown as each source gives them. A second ring main of about 135 km for the wider Chennai Metropolitan Area (763 sq km) is proposed, with its DPR under preparation.
status_history.source_label: MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (Demand No. 34), Government of Tamil Nadu, Aug 2026, pp.204-205 (section 5.2.4)

commitments.title: 24x7 drink-from-tap supply in Kodambakkam and Adyar zones (Rs 1,958 crore)
commitments.committed_by: Government of Tamil Nadu (MAWS) / CMWSSB, with WATCO (Odisha) as nodal agency
commitments.what: Announced in the 2022-23 budget cycle: continuous pressurised drink-from-tap supply in Zone 10 (Kodambakkam) and Zone 13 (Adyar), modelled on Puri. The precursor - a Rs 69.64 crore pilot in Valasaravakkam - was promised complete by June 2023 in the government's policy note. By March 2026 the single-ward trial was spoken of as done and work had begun in Besant Nagar, Adyar, Taramani and Thiruvanmiyur; no public completion date had been given for the two-zone rollout. The state's MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 records the first phase (Pallipattu and Thiruvanmiyur distribution stations) as awarded with a 2-year implementation period, and the remaining stations of Area XIII and Area X to be taken up during 2027-28.

commitment_source.label: MAWS Policy Note 2023-24, p.325 (Valasaravakkam pilot 'expected to be completed by June 2023'); CMWSSB-WATCO MoU week of 17-22 Jul 2023

status_history.note: Valasaravakkam pilot 'nearing completion' in July 2023 (date given: June 2023); CMWSSB signs the implementation MoU with WATCO in the presence of Minister K.N. Nehru.
status_history.source_label: Water Digest, 25 Jul 2023

status_history.note: Valasaravakkam trial described as completed (no commissioning date given in the sources); 24x7 work under way in Besant Nagar, Adyar, Taramani and Thiruvanmiyur via the Pallipattu and Thiruvanmiyur distribution stations; Phase II to extend across Adyar zone and then Kodambakkam - no dates given.
status_history.source_label: Chennaionline, 18 Mar 2026

status_history.note: Checked 18 Oct 2026. The only date on this row, June 2023 for the Valasaravakkam pilot, has passed, and no completion record for the pilot has been found in the board's documents (a March 2026 press report described it as carried out, without a date). The MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (section 5.2.2) gives no completion date for the two-zone rollout: the first phase, 24x7 supply from the Pallipattu and Thiruvanmiyur stations, 'has been awarded under the Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) at an estimated cost of Rs.376.12 crore' with an implementation period of 2 years followed by 15 years of operation and maintenance, for a population of 3.21 lakh; the remaining stations of Area XIII and Area X 'will be taken up during 2027-28', and DPRs for other areas are under preparation. The note gives no award date. With no revised date on record, the row moves from slipped to overdue.
status_history.source_label: MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (Demand No. 34), Government of Tamil Nadu, Aug 2026, p.202

commitments.title: Kosasthalaiyar basin storm drains: 588 km new + 175 km rehabilitated by December 2027
commitments.committed_by: Greater Chennai Corporation / Government of Tamil Nadu, ADB-financed (project 49107-009)
commitments.what: The $470.5 million integrated flood-management project for north Chennai's Kosasthalaiyar basin: 588 km of new storm drains, 175 km rehabilitated, channel improvements at Ambattur, Ariyallur, Kadappakkam and Korattur, to reduce flood exposure for 1.9 million people. ADB approved it on 23 September 2021 with project closing December 2027. GCC's storm-water page (undated, apparently 2023-24 vintage) reported 508 of 769 km complete with the balance 'by March 2024'. The state's MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 recorded 88.39% of the works complete, and the 2026-27 note records the drains as constructed to a length of 769 km.

commitment_source.label: ADB Project Administration Manual, Sept 2021 (closing Dec 2027); ADB approval 23 Sep 2021

status_history.note: GCC's storm-water page (undated; accessed July 2026) reports 508 km of 769 km completed and gives 'by March 2024' for the balance. Note the scope arithmetic also differs: 588+175 = 763 km in the ADB manual versus 769 km on GCC's page. An ADB additional-financing line (49107-012) exists, indicating extension.
status_history.source_label: GCC storm-water department page (undated, accessed Jul 2026)

status_history.note: Ahead of the 2026 civic polls GCC reports 88% of storm-drain works finished city-wide (Rs 6,475 crore, 1,235 km over four years); the same report records residents describing missing links and recurring flooding. The ADB closing date is December 2027; GCC's page had given March 2024 for the balance.
status_history.source_label: Citizen Matters pre-poll report card, 13 Apr 2026

status_history.note: Checked 18 Oct 2026. The MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (section 3.3.3.1, Greater Chennai Corporation) states: 'In the Kosasthalaiyar Basin, Integrated Stormwater Drain has been constructed to a length of 769 km at an estimated cost of Rs.3,059 crore under Asian Development Bank funding.' The two previous notes reported 72.08% complete with completion 'by September 2024' (2024-25) and 88.39% complete (2025-26). This is the state's dated record of the full drain length as built, ahead of the ADB closing date of December 2027. The scope difference in the 2024 entry remains: 769 km here against 588 + 175 = 763 km in the ADB manual.
status_history.source_label: MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (Demand No. 34), Government of Tamil Nadu, Aug 2026, p.105 (section 3.3.3.1); 2025-26 note, p.181

commitments.title: Kannankottai-Thervoy Kandigai reservoir (Chennai's fifth) by 2015
commitments.committed_by: Government of Tamil Nadu / Water Resources Department (announced by CM J. Jayalalithaa, 2012)
commitments.what: A 1 TMC reservoir in Gummidipoondi taluk formed by combining two lakes, filled from the Kandaleru-Poondi (Krishna water) canal, adding ~65 MLD to Chennai. It was announced in 2012 and flagged off in 2013 with a 2015 target; work stopped within a year over land acquisition, ready-dates were later announced (three months away in Feb 2018; next month in Feb 2020), and it was commissioned on 21 November 2020, five years after the 2015 target. Cost: Rs 380 crore plus Rs 160 crore land; it stores water from the existing Krishna entitlement rather than a new source.

commitment_source.label: The News Minute, 1 Mar 2020 (announced 2012, work begun 2013, original target 2015); TN WRD dam page (completed 2020)

status_history.note: WRD says the reservoir will be 'ready in three months'. It was commissioned in November 2020.
status_history.source_label: DT Next, 1 Feb 2018

status_history.note: Commissioned by Union Home Minister Amit Shah with CM Edappadi K. Palaniswami - five years after the original target. First reached full capacity 11 March 2021.
status_history.source_label: The News Minute, 20 Nov 2020

commitments.title: Mamallan reservoir, Kovalam basin (Chennai's sixth) - no completion date given
commitments.committed_by: Government of Tamil Nadu / WRD (Budget 2025-26 announcement; foundation by CM M.K. Stalin)
commitments.what: A ~1.655 TMC drinking-water reservoir between OMR and ECR near Thiruporur, impounding surplus from 69 lakes of the Kovalam basin, meant to supply ~13 lakh people on the IT corridor and double as a flood buffer. Foundation stone laid 19 January 2026. No completion date has been given. Figures on record conflict: cost Rs 471 crore (pre-clearance, May 2025) versus Rs 342.60 crore (at foundation); supply 170 versus 120 MLD; area 4,375 versus 5,161 acres. Fishing communities have raised objections over livelihoods.

commitment_source.label: The Print/PTI, 19 Jan 2026 (foundation stone, Rs 342.60 crore); announced in TN Budget 2025-26 per Deccan Chronicle

status_history.note: Foundation stone laid for the Mamallan reservoir near Nemmeli 'at an estimated cost of Rs 342.60 crore', to supply 17 crore litres a day to Chennai. No completion date is given, so there is no date to measure progress against.
status_history.source_label: The Print/PTI, 19 Jan 2026

status_history.note: Chennaionline reports that construction 'has been temporarily halted', the Water Resources Department stating that the pause is to review the project design and because of recent rain at the Vada Nemmeli site; work is to resume once a high-level committee reports, and Anna University has been asked to validate the designs. It puts the work at 'About 10%' complete, while DT Next (23 Aug 2026) put it at 'Around 30%'; neither figure is attributed to the department. A Citizen Matters report of 2 Oct 2026 describes the work as picking up pace. No completion date has been given. With accounts that conflict and no date, the current status cannot be cited either way.
status_history.source_label: Chennaionline, reporting the Water Resources Department, 2 Sep 2026

commitments.title: Desilt the four city reservoirs to restore 1.904 TMC of storage
commitments.what: Desilting Poondi, Cholavaram and Chembarambakkam (Rs 20.44 crore) plus Red Hills (Rs 9.90 crore) to restore ~1.904 TMC - roughly 45 days of city supply. An earlier version, drawn up after the 2019 drought, set out Rs 36 crore over eight years. The WRD Policy Note 2024-25 records the three-reservoir work 'under implementation' and Red Hills 'to be taken up shortly'; the Policy Note 2025-26 carries the same text a year later, with no completion date or progress figure.

commitment_source.label: WRD Policy Note 2024-25, section 11.0, p.114; Rs 30.5 crore Assembly announcement by Minister Duraimurugan, 21 Jun 2024, per News Today; earlier Rs 36 crore version per Arappor Iyakkam

status_history.note: WRD Policy Note 2025-26, section 11.0 (p.79): the note carries the 2024-25 text: Red Hills 'to be taken up shortly', with no date or progress percentage. Entry date is approximate to the policy note's budget-session tabling.
status_history.source_label: WRD Policy Note 2025-26, p.79

commitments.title: Sholinganallur 54 MLD sewage treatment plant by January 2019
commitments.committed_by: CMWSSB (funded under TNIPP, G.O.(Ms) No.51, MA&WS Dept, 18 Mar 2015)
commitments.what: An SBR plant (18 MLD Module-I + 36 MLD Module-II) serving the Pallikaranai and OMR belt, discharging to the Buckingham Canal. The contract was awarded to the DEE-TECH consortium on 3 March 2016 (Rs 134.44 crore, 30-month term), making the scheduled completion 10 January 2019. CMWSSB's project sheet, dated 1 March 2022, records it 89% complete with September 2022 as the probable finish. The 36 MLD Module-II was inaugurated by CM Stalin on 5 February 2026 (contract completion date 10 January 2019), with the state's 2025-26 policy note recording Module-I as 'has been completed and is under trial run'. CMWSSB's sewerage page and projects list listed the project as pending when accessed in July 2026.

commitment_source.label: CMWSSB project sheet (contract 03.03.2016, 30-month term; progress as on 01.03.2022)

status_history.note: 89% complete as on 1 March 2022 (contract completion date 10 January 2019); CMWSSB's sheet gives September 2022 as the probable completion including trial runs.
status_history.source_label: CMWSSB project sheet, progress as on 01.03.2022

status_history.note: CM Stalin inaugurates the 36 MLD Sholinganallur plant (Module-II of this project) among Metro Water works worth Rs 635.31 crore; the project's contract completion date was 10 January 2019. The MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 (section 5.3.4) records the 18 MLD Module-I as 'has been completed and is under trial run'. CMWSSB's sewerage page and projects list listed the project as pending when accessed 5 Jul 2026.
status_history.source_label: DT Next, 5 Feb 2026; MAWS Policy Note 2025-26, section 5.3.4

status_history.note: The state's MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (section 5.3.2, Table 5.4) lists Sholinganallur at 72 MLD (18+18+36) in Chennai's installed sewage treatment capacity; the 2025-26 note had listed Sholinganallur I at 18 MLD.
status_history.source_label: MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (Demand No. 34), Government of Tamil Nadu, Aug 2026, p.209 (Table 5.4); 2025-26 note, p.316 (Table 5.4)

commitments.title: Raise Chennai's sewage treatment capacity to 951 MLD by 31 December 2021
commitments.committed_by: Government of Tamil Nadu (Additional Chief Secretary), in a sworn quarterly report to the NGT (OA 606/2018)
commitments.what: In its December 2020 quarterly compliance report to the National Green Tribunal, Tamil Nadu committed to raising Chennai's treatment capacity to 951 MLD by 31 December 2021 (Rs 636 crore of rehabilitation and new plants). The state's MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 records 957.80 MLD installed, roughly two to three years after that date, with the Kodungaiyur I and II, Nesapakkam and Perungudi plants 'have been inaugurated by Hon'ble Chief Minister in 2023-24 & 2024-25 and are in operation'; the 2026-27 note records 1,031.80 MLD. CMWSSB's sewerage page (last reviewed 18 March 2024) gives 745 MLD, and its plant table does not yet include the four new plants (accessed July and October 2026).

commitment_source.label: TN Quarterly Report for December 2020 to NGT, OA 606/2018 (951 MLD by 31.12.2021)

status_history.note: NGT's order records TN's submission that Chennai's capacity 'attained' 912.80 MLD by October 2022, ten months after the 31 December 2021 date, against the 951 MLD target, with a further 304 MLD committed (Rs 536.19 crore, AMRUT/TNIPP), no due date attached.
status_history.source_label: NGT order of 17 Nov 2022, OA 606/2018 (State of Tamil Nadu)

status_history.note: The state's MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 (section 5.3.2-5.3.3): installed capacity 957.80 MLD, with Kodungaiyur I & II (120+120), Nesapakkam (50) and Perungudi (60) 'have been inaugurated by Hon'ble Chief Minister in 2023-24 & 2024-25 and are in operation'. 951 MLD was reached roughly 2-3 years after the date; the note gives fiscal years rather than inauguration dates. Entry date is the date of the note's PDF.
status_history.source_label: MAWS Policy Note 2025-26, pp.316-318 (Table 5.4)

status_history.note: CMWSSB's sewerage page, fetched this date, gives 'the present capacity of the treatment plant is 745 MLD', and its plant table does not list the four new NGT-era plants; the state's MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 gives 957.80 MLD.
status_history.source_label: CMWSSB Sewerage System page, accessed 5 Jul 2026

status_history.note: The state's MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (section 5.3.2, Table 5.4) records installed sewage treatment capacity of 1,031.80 MLD, up from 957.80 MLD in the 2025-26 note, and section 5.3.3 records the 4 new STPs (Kodungaiyur I and II, Perungudi, Nesapakkam) and the rehabilitation of 7 existing STPs as completed at a cost of Rs 923.95 crore.
status_history.source_label: MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (Demand No. 34), Government of Tamil Nadu, Aug 2026, pp.209-210 (Table 5.4, section 5.3.3); 2025-26 note, p.316

commitments.title: Eco-restoration of the Cooum (32 km, ~60 sub-projects)
commitments.committed_by: Chennai Rivers Restoration Trust (CRRT) / Government of Tamil Nadu
commitments.what: The Integrated Cooum River Eco-Restoration Project has run since 2015 (administrative sanction Rs 735.08 crore; in 2017 CRRT hoped to complete in three years, i.e. ~2020). The state's status report to the NGT (as on 30 June 2021) carried sub-project deadlines through 2021-22 for sewage interception, modular STPs and resettlement. The state's MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (p.298) records Rs 613.29 crore disbursed of the Rs 735.08 crore sanction, and all restoration works completed except the resettlement of the remaining 773 families at 7 locations. By June 2024, 37 of 118 identified sewage outfalls were plugged and 13,481 of 14,257 families resettled; Ground Report (10 Jun 2024) put spending at Rs 735 crore. In CPCB's October 2025 assessment (2022-23 data), the Cooum from Poonamallee to Central Jail is a Priority I polluted river stretch, CPCB's highest-priority class, with maximum BOD of 180 mg/l at Arumbakkam. No revised whole-project date has been given; the 2026-27 note proposes a new Cooum and Adyar programme through Chennai Rivers Transformation Company Limited, with global tenders and a DPR.

commitments.title: Adyar river restoration (42 km, Rs 744.60 crore), and the Rs 1,500 crore PPP that followed
commitments.committed_by: Chennai Rivers Restoration Trust (CRRT) / Government of Tamil Nadu
commitments.what: Works began in 2018 under a Rs 744.60 crore sanction. No overall completion date was published, so the due date here is the latest sub-deadline in the state's status report to the NGT (Anakaputhur and Pammal UGSS, expected May 2023); we label that derivation openly. In January 2023 TNPCB recorded no dissolved oxygen at 23 locations on the river. A Rs 1,500 crore 'One River, One Operator' PPP under a hybrid-annuity DBFOT model followed: its CMWSSB concessionaire tender closed 30 November 2023 and it has featured in successive state budgets from 2024-25 (Rs 300 crore in 2025-26). No concession award had been reported as of July 2026. The state's MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 records that a project to restore the Adyar on the Hybrid Annuity Model, sanctioned on 14.03.2024, 'could not take-off due to contractual issues' (p.300); it records Rs 571.66 crore disbursed of the Rs 744.60 crore sanction, with most works completed except one CMWSSB work and the resettlement of 3,236 families (p.299), and proposes a new Adyar and Cooum programme through Chennai Rivers Transformation Company Limited, with global tenders and a DPR (pp.301-303). CPCB's October 2025 assessment keeps the Adyar in Priority I, its highest-priority class.

commitments.title: Buckingham Canal: demarcate in 6 months, then clear encroachments in 1 year (Madras HC, 12 Sept 2022)
commitments.committed_by: Government of Tamil Nadu / PWD-WRD / Greater Chennai Corporation, under Madras High Court order in W.P.No.6609 of 2014
commitments.what: On 12 September 2022 the Madras High Court's First Bench (Chief Justice Munishwar Nath Bhandari and Justice N. Mala) ordered the canal's boundaries demarcated within six months - 'under no circumstance, the time line will be extended' - and encroachments removed within one year of demarcation completing. The demarcation window set by the court closed around March 2023 with about 40% demarcated; the one-year period for removing encroachments runs from the completion of demarcation. In November 2024 the state announced that restoration components in Chepauk-Triplicane and Mylapore would not proceed, citing a severe shortage of funds. The canal's carrying capacity has fallen from 5,600 to 2,850 cusecs; the MRTS line was built along the canal. In June 2026 the Centre gave in-principle approval to Rs 7,500 crore for the Cooum, Adyar and Buckingham Canal under the Urban Challenge Fund, with DPRs to follow in stages. The register will record the demarcation's completion when a dated source reports it.

status_history.note: The demarcation window set by the court closed around March 2023 with about 40% demarcated (northern and southern stretches); the encroachment-removal year runs from the completion of demarcation. commitments.title: Restore the Kodungaiyur 45 MLD recycled-water plant to full output in 18 months
commitments.committed_by: CMWSSB, via PPP contract with VA Tech Wabag
commitments.what: Chennai built two 45 MLD tertiary treatment (TTRO) plants to sell recycled water to industry. The state's MAWS Policy Note 2023-24 recorded them running at 23 MLD (Kodungaiyur) and 15 MLD (Koyambedu). In March 2026 CMWSSB awarded Wabag a refurbish-finance-operate-transfer contract reported at over Rs 1,000 crore to bring Kodungaiyur back to its full 45 MLD within 18 months, plus 18.5 years of operation. The plant was commissioned in 2019. The state's MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 records the PPP refurbishment as commenced and 'to be completed by 2028'.

commitment_source.label: Indian Chemical News, 14 Mar 2026 (Wabag PPP award, 18-month restoration); output figures per MAWS Policy Note 2023-24, p.318

status_history.note: CMWSSB issues a Letter of Award to VA Tech Wabag for a public-private partnership to refurbish, finance, operate, maintain and transfer the 45 MLD TTRO plant at Kodungaiyur: restore its full 45 MLD capacity 'within 18 months', then operate and maintain it for 18.5 years.

status_history.note: The MAWS Policy Note 2026-27 (section 5.5.2.1) records that the refurbishment, operation and maintenance of the plant through PPP 'has commenced and to be completed by 2028'. update_model: Statuses change only against a dated citation. The register is re-checked against a small calendar of documents: the MAWS Policy Note each year (the richest single source of CMWSSB's own targets; the 2026-27 note's PDF is dated 21 August 2026), ADB project documents for the ring main and Kosasthalaiyar drains, and CMWSSB/ministerial announcements reported in DT Next and The Hindu. Each commitment carries a next-check date; a passed next-check prompts a re-check.
sources_note: Sources are the institutions' own documents wherever they exist (MAWS Policy Notes, CMWSSB board policy, ADB loan documents, contractor releases) and dated reporting where they do not. Where figures conflict (Perur's costs, the ring main's price tags, drain kilometres, the Cooum's spending) each is shown with its label. Claims we could not verify, such as the Minjur November 2024 shutdown, are named as unverified. Entries citing a MAWS Policy Note are dated by the note's PDF, since the notes print no tabling date: 22 March 2025 for the 2025-26 note and 21 August 2026 for the 2026-27 note. Entries citing the 2023-24 note carry 15 April 2023, an approximate tabling date.
